Asia reversed the 'Black Tuesday' KOSPI panic: KOSPI +5.42% to 8,930, Nikkei 225 +4.61% to 72,366. ES futures +0.7%, NQ +2.1% as of 6:25 AM EDT. Oil extends its decline (WTI $69.42, Brent ~$73) — the most powerful near-term disinflation input heading into today's May PCE print. Verdict remains HOLD at medium conviction because three regime indicators are still breached pre-open: VIX premarket ~18.32 (above 17 gate, down from 19.49 close), DXY 101.27 (above 100 gate), and ES futures imply an SPX open of ~7,409 — still 51 pts below the 7,460 floor. PCE releases at 8:30 AM ET (consensus: 4.1% YoY headline / 3.3% core); Q1 GDP Third Estimate also at 8:30 AM ET. Cold PCE core below 3.2% → HOLD upgrades to BUY same session. Hot core above 3.5% → trim new MU/NVDA adds within 45 minutes. BTC at $61,285 remains below the $63,500 exit gate.

bear_case: Counter-argument: the MU and QCOM confirmations represent hardware-layer AI demand — they do not change the monetary policy framework. BofA's 3-hike forecast (Sep/Oct/Dec 2026) and Deutsche Bank's September hike addition predate both catalysts and remain the dominant rate pricing input. If May PCE prints 4.1% YoY headline and 3.3% core — exactly consensus — the 30Y tests 5.00%, DXY resumes its rise, and the AI multiple compression that began June 22 continues regardless of Micron's $50B guide. The KOSPI +5.42% recovery does not undo the structural MSCI reweighting that triggered the June 23 panic; it reflects one session of technical relief. More telling: MU gave back its entire AH surge by morning ($1,083 premarket vs $1,199 AH high), and NVDA did not gap meaningfully higher on MU's $50B Q4 guide — the market is not ready to pay up on AI hardware before the rate regime clears. Q1 GDP Third Estimate at 8:30 AM ET (prior: 1.6% annualized, downward-revised from 2.0%) adds a growth-softening data point that could complicate the risk-on narrative. Invalidation: PCE core above 3.5% → HOLD reverts to STEP ASIDE; trim MU/NVDA within 45 minutes. If SPX fails to reclaim 7,460 by June 25 close even on a cold PCE print, the regime breach is structural and BEARISH framework extends into Q3.
